idiom_name: sealed interface + record variants + switch with record patterns
implementation_notes: Sealed interfaces close the variant set with the permits clause, records supply the product half (accessors, equals/hashCode, deconstruction), and switch patterns over a sealed selector are exhaustive without a default arm - the compiler knows every permitted subtype. Record patterns deconstruct payloads right in the case label. This is the OO encoding of a sum type with language-level coverage checking; Java 21 is the floor because pattern matching for switch was finalized there (sealed types since 17, records since 16).
pitfalls: Exhaustiveness is a compile-time claim: if the sealed hierarchy is recompiled to permit a new subtype while the switching class is not, the switch throws MatchException at run time - recompile together.

Pattern labels are checked for dominance; a broad type pattern placed before a specific one is a compile error, and a null selector still throws NullPointerException unless a 'case null' label exists.
Records are shallowly immutable: an array or mutable collection component can still be mutated, which breaks the value semantics the variant assumes.

variants.name: Closed abstract-class hierarchy + Visitor (Java 8)
variants.idiom_name: abstract base with private constructor + nested final variants + Visitor
variants.implementation_notes: Before sealed types, closure was simulated: the base class keeps a private or package-private constructor so no other source file can extend it, each variant is a static nested final class, and the operation lives either as an abstract method on the base or in a Visitor when operations change more often than variants. The compiler cannot prove coverage, so every dispatch ends in a default that throws. Choose this only on Java 8-17 toolchains, or when new operations (not new variants) dominate and Visitor's double dispatch is the smaller cost.
pitfalls: Closure by private constructor is a convention the compiler only half-enforces: reflection, serialization frameworks and instrumentation can still create instances, and a mistake in the modifier silently opens the set.
Without pattern matching, dispatch is an if/else instanceof chain whose default branch is the only exhaustiveness signal - it fires at run time, not at compile time.
Visitor inverts the extension axis: adding a variant means editing every visitor, so do not choose it when the variant set is the thing that grows.
